newsitem.title: USA: Lyondell sets HDPE production increase.
newsitem.headline: Lyondell sets HDPE production increase.

text.p: Lyondell Petrochemical Co said Monday it plans to add 440 million pounds of Nissan Chemical Industries Ltd technology high density polyethylene (HDPE) resin capacity with a targeted start up no later than mid-1999.
The company said it is evaluating locations for the unit.
Initial spending for the project is included in Lyondell's 1997 capital budget, which totalls $132 million, it said.
This compares to spending of $130 million last year, a spokesman said. The company also joined Citgo in spending $473 million on an upgrade of their refinery.

Lyondell said the expansion will build on its position as a leading supplier of high-molecular-weight HDPE film resins. It will bring the company's total HDPE capacity to more than two billion pounds, making it one of the world's leading producers.

The "expansion will provide us with capacity to supply the rapidly growing film market where we are a strong participant, and also benefits our olefins business through additional vertical integration," chief executive Dan F. Smith said.
The increasing rate of demand for high-molecular weight film resin is expected to outpace the growth rate of other resins, Lyondell said.
These resins are used primarily in grocery and merchandise carry-out bags as well as industrial and consumer trash bags.

The Nissan technology, already in use at the company's Matagorda County, Texas, plant, provides Lyondell with a competitive economic advantage. Lyondell noted it also promotes licensing of the Nissan technology under a joint agreement with Nissan Chemical and Maruzen Polymer.

The 440 million pound expansion will provide the company with 40 percent more capacity to meet the projected growth of its film customers, as well as incremental capacity for blow molding, injection molding and pipe markets.

Currently, Lyondell's annual HDPE capacity includes 1.1 billion pounds at the Matagorda plant and 475 million pounds at a plant in Victoria, Texas. A recently announced debottlenecking project at Victoria will increase capacity at that site to 575 million pounds by 1998.

At a plant in LaPorte, Texas, Lyondell recently completed a 100 million pound expansion of polypropylene capacity, bringing its total to 400 million pounds. At that facility, Lyondell also operates a low-density polyethylene unit with annual capacity of 150 million pounds.

Other major projects in the 1997 capital budget include the debottlenecking of the Victoria HDPE capacity, and control and electrical upgrades at the Channelview Petrochemical Complex and Lyondell-Citgo Refining Co Ltd.
